unsupported_claims: First-order proximity "models the symmetric similarity between the two endpoints of each observed edge" - this elaboration is not stated in the provided evidence, though it is consistent with the LINE paper's general background.
Second-order proximity "models the similarity of neighborhood structures" - also an elaboration not in the evidence excerpts.
rationale: The core claims are supported: the first-order variants (LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st)) only apply to undirected graphs, while the second-order variants apply to both directed and undirected graphs. The extra descriptions of what each proximity models are standard, uncontroversial background from the LINE paper, so they do not count against the answer. The answer is somewhat vague in saying "the first-order variant" without naming both LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st), but it implies both.
